grh_e68f5b2d4f5273dc3ae1.title: Lorna Doone
paragraphs: John Ridd loves Lorna, a young woman held among the outlaw Doones and claimed by the violent Carver Doone. When Lorna refuses Carver, the clan abandons her to starve and John crosses the dangerous country to rescue her. Carver confronts them and reveals that Lorna was kidnapped as a child and is not a Doone by blood, removing the family barrier between her and John. During their final struggle Carver loses his footing and plunges from a cliff. With the threat gone, Lorna promises to remain with John for the rest of her life.

Lee as radio adaptor, Gordon MacRae as host, and Marvin Miller as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.f7185f50dd01455d|Association of American Railroads]].
This version dramatizes [[work|work.rr.3ccf767c8dd77062|Lorna Doone]]. R. D. Blackmore is credited as author, Jerome Lawrence adapted it for radio, and Robert E. Lee adapted it for radio.

grh_e66d96ce3f25cf190ba6.title: Miss Lizzies Burglar
paragraphs: Miss Lizzie surprises a burglar named Joe in her home, but instead of turning the injured man over to the police she nurses him back toward health. Joe, who boasts that he has avoided women all his life, becomes increasingly terrified that her kindness and concern mean she intends to marry him, and finally tries to escape before he is trapped. Dr. Christian is called into the absurd quarrel and discovers that both have misunderstood the other. Miss Lizzie has indeed been hoping to keep Joe, but not as a husband: what she desperately wants is a landscape gardener, and Joe happens to be one. The marriage panic collapses into a much more practical job offer.

The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_e63e7636aa9561de8d9c.title: The Troublemaker
paragraphs: An electronics company hires an outside troubleshooter to fix a management team whose three senior executives blame one another for every problem. Instead of smoothing things over, he deliberately needles each man, exposing a martini-soaked decision maker, an overbearing ego and a boss whose temper drives away employees. His provocations finally give the three executives a common enemy and force them to unite in defense of one another. Once the chairman fires the apparent troublemaker, the consultant reveals that getting the team to stop fighting each other and work together was the real assignment.
